declarations.name: AuiSortableList

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Accessible name of the list (aria-label on the <ul>). Must be non-empty after trimming.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Items in order. Ids must be unique, non-empty, and stable; labels non-empty (used in the handle name and announcements). Rows are kept by id on update; the array order defines the DOM order.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable reordering for the whole list (all handles disabled).

inputs.name: dragFrom
inputs.description: Where a pointer drag can start: the handle only, or anywhere on a movable item (interactive content inside the item keeps its own pointer behavior).

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Dispatched on the host after a keyboard or pointer drop that changed the item's position. from and to are zero-based. Not emitted for cancels, drops in place, move(), or update().

properties.name: isDragging
properties.description: Read-only: Whether an item is grabbed (keyboard) or dragged (pointer).

methods.name: move
methods.description: Move an item to a zero-based index; cancels an active grab or drag first. No event, no announcement. Throws SORTABLE_LIST_OPTIONS for an unknown id or an index outside 0..count-1.

accessibility.pattern: Reorderable list with a toggle-button grab handle per item and live-region announcements (keyboard drag-and-drop pattern). Native list semantics; no ARIA drag-and-drop attributes (aria-grabbed and aria-dropeffect are deprecated).

limitations: No auto-scroll during a pointer drag; the dragged item is clamped to the list's visible bounds.
No drag between lists and no nesting.
update() and global configuration changes re-render in the order of the items option; after a reorder, pass the new order back with update({ items }) or the DOM order reverts on the next re-render.
Item content is inserted once per item and re-inserted only when the item's content (or, without content, its label) changes by identity.
Announcements are English by default; register messages for other locales.
Every pointer-driven position change is announced assertively, which can be verbose while dragging over many items.
